h: The Gift of Rest and the Inner Holiness of Shabbat
Shabbat rest is more than cessation from work: it is a revelation of divine holiness within Israel.
Rest as the Expression of Inward Sanctity

p: יוֹם מְנוּחָה וּקְדוּשָׁה לְעַמְּךָ נָתַתָּ".
"A day of rest and holiness You have given unto Your people."
בַּגְּמָרָא:
In the Gemara: "
מַתָּנָה טוֹבָה יֵשׁ לִי בְּבֵית גְּנָזַי וְשַׁבָּת שְׁמָהּ" וְכוּלֵי.
"'A good gift I have in My treasure-house and Shabbat is its name,' etc."
וְאָמַרְנוּ שֶׁהַמַּתָּנָה טוֹבָה הִיא מַה שֶׁנָּתַן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַכֹּחַ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
And we explained that the 'good gift' is that Hashem gave power unto Israel
לְהַכְנִיס קְדוּשָּׁה לַשַּׁבָּת עַל יְדֵי שֶׁנָּתַן בָּהֶם קְדוּשָּׁה.
to introduce sanctity into Shabbat by placing holiness within them.
אַךְ לְפִי זֶה אֵינוֹ מְדוּקְדָּק לְשׁוֹן הַגְּמָרָא "וְשַׁבָּת שְׁמָהּ".
However, according to this, the phrasing of the Gemara 'and Shabbat is its name' is not precise.
וְיִתָּכֵן דְּקָאֵי עַל הַמְּנוּחָה שֶׁנָּתַן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
And it is possible that it refers to the rest that He gave to Israel,
שֶׁיְּהֵא נִיחָא בַּלֵּב.
that there be spiritual tranquility in the heart.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר "וְשַׁבָּת שְׁמָהּ"
– And this is why it says 'and Shabbat is its name'—
לְשׁוֹן נִיחָא וּמְנוּחָה.
an expression of tranquility and rest.
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶׁכָּתוּב (בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק א, מח עַמּוּד ב)
And it is based on what is written (in the holy Zohar Part I, 48b)
דְּדָרַשׁ "בְּיוֹם הָנִיחַ ה' לְךָ מֵעָצְבְּךָ וְגוֹמֵר"
which expounds the verse 'on the day Hashem gives you rest from your sorrow, etc.'
עַל יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת.
as referring to the Sabbath day.
וְהוּא מִדִּכְתִיב "בְּיוֹם הָנִיחַ" וְלֹא כְתִיב "בַּהֲנִיחַ",
And this is derived because it is written 'on the day He gives rest' and not merely 'when He gives rest',
וּמִזֶּה דָּרַשׁ דְּקָאֵי עַל יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁהוּא יוֹם מְנוּחָה.
and from this it expounded that it refers to the Sabbath day which is a day of rest.
וְלֹא יְצוּיַּר שֶׁיִּשְׁכַּח כָּל צַעֲרוֹ
And it cannot be conceived that a person should forget all his agony
אַף שֶׁהוּא עוֹד בַּעֲבוֹדָה קָשָׁה,
even while he is still in the midst of harsh labor,
רַק כְּשֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹתֵן הַמְּנוּחָה בַּלֵּב בְּמַתָּנָה
unless Hashem, blessed be He, grants rest in the heart as a direct gift,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא שָׁבַת מִכָּל מְלַאכְתּוֹ,
just as He rested from all His work.
שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ נִיחָא בְּשַׁבָּת מִכָּל הַבְּרִיאָה
For He had satisfaction on Shabbat from all Creation,
אַף מִמַּה שֶּׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ הַטּוֹב,
even from that which appears as the opposite of good,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁדָּרַשׁ בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה עַל הַפָּסוּק
as Bereishit Rabbah expounds on the verse: "
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה וְהִנֵּה טוֹב מְאֹד",
"'And God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good,'
כֵּן נוֹתֵן בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל הַנִּיחָא מִכָּל הַהֵיפֶךְ גַּם כֵּן.
so does He place within the heart of Israel tranquility from all opposite adversity as well.
וְלִפְעָמִים יְצוּיַּר
And at times it could be imagined
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי שֶׁאוֹכֵל וְשׁוֹתֶה וּמִתְעַנֵּג בְּשַׁבָּת
that through eating, drinking, and indulging in Shabbat,
וְקוֹבֵעַ סְעוּדָתוֹ עַל הַיַּיִן כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת מב.),
and fixing one's meal over wine, as written (Berakhot 42a),
יִשְׁתֶּה וְיִשְׁכַּח רֵישׁוֹ וְכָל הַצַּעַר שֶׁלּוֹ.
he drinks and forgets his poverty and all of his agony.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר הַכָּתוּב: "לָדַעַת כִּי אֲנִי ה' מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם,
And regarding this Scripture states: 'To know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you,
מַתָּנָה טוֹבָה יֵשׁ לִי בְּבֵית גְּנָזַי וְשַׁבָּת שְׁמָהּ
a good gift I have in My treasure-house and Shabbat is its name,
וַאֲנִי מְבַקֵּשׁ לִיתְּנָהּ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל".
and I wish to give it unto Israel.'
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַנִּיחָא יִהְיֶה עַל יְדֵי שֶׁנִּיתַּן בָּהֶם קְדוּשָּׁה,
Namely, that this tranquility comes about because holiness was placed within them,
שֶׁמַּכִּירִין שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
in that they recognize that everything is from Hashem, blessed be He,
וְהוּא צוֹפֶה לְטוֹבָה תָּמִיד.
and He is always watching for the ultimate good.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יֵשׁ לוֹ נִיחָא מִכָּל צַעַר,
And through this he possesses tranquility from all distress, "
מֵעָצְבְּךָ וּמֵרָגְזֶךָ"
– from 'your sorrow and your turmoil'—
הַיְינוּ מֵעֶצֶב הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
namely from the depression of the evil inclination,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ (תְּמוּרָה טז.):
as is expounded (Temurah 16a): "
לְבִלְתִּי עָצְבִּי" – שֶׁלֹּא יַשְׂגִּיבַנִי הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע מִלִּשְׁנוֹת וְכוּלֵי;
"'that it may not grieve me'—lest the evil inclination prevent me from reviewing my learning, etc.;"
וְרוֹגֶז הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְהַרְגִּיז עָלָיו הַיֵּצֶר הַטּוֹב (בְּרָכוֹת ה.);
and the turmoil of the evil inclination, over which one must agitate the good inclination (Berakhot 5a); "
וּמִן הָעֲבֹדָה הַקָּשָׁה אֲשֶׁר עֻבַּד בָּךְ"
– and 'from the hard labor which was worked upon you'—
שֶׁאַף שֶׁהוּא עוֹד בְּתוֹךְ הָעֲבוֹדָה הַקָּשָׁה,
that even while one is still immersed in the arduous labor,
אַף עַל פִּי כֵן יִהְיֶה לוֹ נִיחָא
he will nonetheless have tranquility
מֵחֲמַת שֶׁמַּכִּיר שֶׁהוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְהוּא לְטוֹבָה.
because he recognizes that it is from Hashem, blessed be He, and is for the good.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכָה מֵעֵין שֶׁבַע:
And this is what we recite in the blessing of Me'ein Sheva: "
וּמֵנִיחַ בִּקְדוּשָׁה לְעַם מְדוּשְּׁנֵי עֹנֶג",
"and grants rest in holiness to a people laden with delight,"
שֶׁהַנִּיחָא עַל יְדֵי הַקְּדוּשָּׁה שֶׁנּוֹתֵן בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל.
for the tranquility arises through the holiness that He places within the heart of Israel.
וּבְבִרְכַּת קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע:
And in the blessing preceding the Shema: "
שֶׁבַח יְקָר וּגְדוּלָּה וְכָבוֹד יִתְּנוּ לָאֵל מֶלֶךְ יוֹצֵר כֹּל",
"Praise, glory, greatness, and honor shall they render unto God, King, Former of all,"
שֶׁעַל זֶה יִתְּנוּ שֶׁבַח מְיוּחָד,
for over this they render unique praise,
שֶׁהוּא יוֹצֵר כֹּל שֶׁמּוֹרֶה עַל הֵיפֶךְ מֵהַטּוֹב,
in that He is 'Former of all,' which points even to the opposite of good,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁתִּקְּנוּ בִּמְקוֹם "וּבוֹרֵא רָע" וְקָרִינַן "הַכֹּל".
as they formulated euphemistically in place of 'and Creator of evil,' reciting 'all.' "
הַמַּנְחִיל מְנוּחָה לְעַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּקְדוּשָׁתוֹ בְּיוֹם שַׁבַּת קֹדֶשׁ",
"'Who bequeaths rest unto His people Israel in His holiness on the holy Sabbath day,'
שֶׁנּוֹתֵן הַמְּנוּחָה עַל יְדֵי הַקְּדוּשָּׁה שֶׁמּוֹפִיעַ בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל
for He grants rest through the holiness that shines into the heart of Israel,
וְלֹא עַל יְדֵי יַיִן וְכַדּוֹמֶה.
and not through wine and the like.
וְזֶה נוֹתֵן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּנַחֲלָה וִירֻשָּׁה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ הֶפְסֵק (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכט:).
And this He gives unto Israel as an inheritance and heritage that knows no interruption (Bava Batra 129b).
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּקִידּוּשׁ:
And this is what we recite in Kiddush: "
וְשַׁבַּת קָדְשׁוֹ בְּאַהֲבָה וּבְרָצוֹן הִנְחִילָנוּ" וְכוּלֵי, "הִנְחַלְתָּנוּ",
"'and His holy Sabbath He bequeathed to us in love and favor, etc., You bequeathed unto us,'
שֶׁהַנִּיחָא הִנְחִיל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדֵי הָאַהֲבָה וְרָצוֹן.
for the tranquility He bequeathed to Israel through love and favor.
שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל נִיחָא בְּכָל הָעוֹבֵר עָלָיו,
Such that a Jew has tranquility amidst all that passes over him,
שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ וּמַכִּיר שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַצּוֹפֶה לְטוֹבָה,
knowing and recognizing that everything is from Hashem, blessed be He, Who watches for good, "
וּכְאָב אֶת בֵּן יִרְצֶה".
'and as a father delights in the son.'
וְכֵן בַּתְּפִלָּה: "לְיִשְׂרָאֵל עַמְּךָ נְתַתּוֹ בְּאַהֲבָה, לְזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב",
And so in prayer: 'Unto Israel Your people You gave it in love, to the seed of Jacob,'
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַׁת יַעֲקֹב זָכוּ לְנַחֲלָה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ הֶפְסֵק,
for through the holiness of Jacob they merited an uninterrupted heritage,
שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ "אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב"
whose attribute is 'truth to Jacob,'
וּ"שְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד".
and 'the lip of truth shall be established forever.'
וּבְיוֹם טוֹב אוֹמְרִים: "וּמוֹעֲדֵי קָדְשְׁךָ בְּשִׂמְחָה וּבְשָׂשׂוֹן הִנְחַלְתָּנוּ".
And on Yom Tov we say: 'and Your holy appointed seasons in gladness and joy You bequeathed unto us.'
דְּשִׂמְחָה יָכוֹל לִהְיוֹת שֶׁל הוֹלֵלוּת,
For joy can potentially degenerate into frivolity;
וְרַק כֵּיוָן שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹתֵן הַשִּׂמְחָה וְשָׂשׂוֹן בַּלֵּב בְּנַחֲלָה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ הֶפְסֵק,
and only because Hashem grants joy and gladness in the heart as an uninterrupted heritage,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה הַשִּׂמְחָה הוּא בִּקְדוּשָׁה,
thereby the joy is sanctified in holiness, "
שִׂמְחוּ בַּה'", "יִשְׂמַח יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעֹשָׂיו".
'Rejoice in Hashem,' 'Let Israel rejoice in its Maker.'
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ בְּמַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְהָיִיתָ אַךְ שָׂמֵחַ",
And as we explained regarding the verse: 'and you shall be solely joyful,'
שֶׁהוּא הַבְטָחָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַשִּׂמְחָה בִּקְדוּשָׁה בְּצִמְצוּם,
that it is a promise that joy will be in holiness with measured restraint, "
אַךְ" לְשׁוֹן מִיעוּט, שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה שִׂמְחָה שֶׁל הוֹלֵלוּת.
'solely' (akh) being an exclusionary term, ensuring it is not a frivolous joy.
וּבִתְפִלָּה דְּרַחֲמֵי נִינְהוּ מְבַקְּשִׁים:
And in prayer, which is a plea for mercy, we beseech: "
וְהַנְחִילֵנוּ ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ בְּאַהֲבָה וּבְרָצוֹן שַׁבַּת קָדְשֶׁךָ",
'And bequeath unto us, Hashem our God, in love and favor Your holy Sabbath,'
אַף דִּבְקִידּוּשׁ נוֹתְנִים הוֹדָאָה עַל הֶעָבָר: "וְשַׁבַּת קָדְשְׁךָ בְּאַהֲבָה וּבְרָצוֹן הִנְחִילָנוּ, הִנְחַלְתָּנוּ".
even though in Kiddush we render thanksgiving over the past: 'and Your holy Sabbath in love and favor He bequeathed / You bequeathed unto us.'
וְלָמָּה מְבַקְּשִׁים עַל זֶה?
Why then do we plead for this?
בִּשְׁלָמָא בְּעִנְיַן קְדוּשָׁה, דְּאָמְרִינַן בְּקִידּוּשָׁא "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ",
It is understandable regarding holiness, where we recite in Kiddush 'Who has sanctified us',
דִּבִּצְלוֹתָא "קַדְּשֵׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתֶיךָ" מַאי טַעְמָא?
and in the prayer we say 'Sanctify us with Your commandments'—for what reason?
דְּרַחֲמֵי נִינְהוּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא (פְּסָחִים קיז:),
Because it is an appeal for mercy, as written in the Gemara (Pesachim 117b),
לָא קַשְׁיָא,
this is not difficult,
דִּבִּקְדוּשָׁה יֵשׁ הַרְבֵּה מַדְרֵיגוֹת,
for in holiness there are numerous ascending levels,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (חֻלִּין ז.): "יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים הֵם",
as written (Chullin 7a): 'Israel are holy,'
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם רַבִּי נִקְרָא "רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ" (שַׁבָּת קיח:), שֶׁהָיָה קוֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים,
and nevertheless Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi was termed 'our holy teacher' (Shabbat 118b), having been holy of holies,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמַר רַבִּי עַל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
and yet Rabbi said concerning Rabbi Yosi
שֶׁהוּא כְּחוֹלֵי חוּלִין לְקָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים לְגַבֵּי דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
that he is like non-sacred dust compared to holy of holies relative to Rabbi Yosi,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי סוֹף פֶּרֶק ו דְּגִיטִּין),
as written (Yerushalmi Gittin 6:7 end);
עַל כֵּן יִתָּכֵן לְהִתְפַּלֵּל עַל קְדוּשָׁה
therefore it is fitting to pray for higher holiness
אַף שֶׁמּוֹדִים עַל הֶעָבָר "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ".
even while giving thanks over the past 'Who has sanctified us.'
אֲבָל לְהִתְפַּלֵּל "וְהַנְחִילֵנוּ ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ בְּאַהֲבָה וּבְרָצוֹן שַׁבַּת קָדְשֶׁךָ"
However, to plead 'And bequeath unto us, Hashem our God, in love and favor Your holy Sabbath'
אַחַר שֶׁכְּבָר נוֹתְנִים הוֹדָאָה עַל הֶעָבָר "הִנְחִילָנוּ, הִנְחַלְתָּנוּ"
after having already given thanks over the past 'He bequeathed / You bequeathed unto us'
אֵינוֹ מוּבָן.
is difficult to understand.
אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת גַּם בְּהַנִּיחָא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ הַרְבֵּה מַדְרֵיגוֹת,
Yet in truth, within the tranquility possessed by Israel there are also many gradations,
וְכָל אֶחָד כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁזּוֹכֶה
and each individual, according to what he merits,
מַרְגִּישׁ הַמְּנוּחָה וְהַנִּיחָא בַּלֵּב בְּשַׁבָּת,
feels the rest and inner tranquility in the heart on Shabbat;
וְעַל זֶה מִתְפַּלְּלִין "וְהַנְחִילֵנוּ" וְכוּלֵי.
and over this we pray 'and bequeath unto us, etc.'
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל זוֹכֶה לְנִיחָא בְּשַׁבָּת
Yet nonetheless, every single Jew merits tranquility on Shabbat,
וְזֶה הַמַּתָּנָה טוֹבָה "וְשַׁבָּת שְׁמָהּ".
and this is the good gift of 'and Shabbat is its name.'
וְעַל זֶה מוֹדִים בְּקִידּוּשׁ,
And over this we give thanks in Kiddush,
וְזֶהוּ "יוֹם מְנוּחָה וּקְדוּשָׁה לְעַמְּךָ נָתַתָּ" בְּמַתָּנָה,
and this is 'A day of rest and holiness You gave unto Your people' as a gift,
שֶׁיְּהֵא הַמְּנוּחָה בִּקְדוּשָׁה עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַׁת הַשַּׁבָּת.
that the rest be enveloped in holiness through the holiness of Shabbat.
וְחוֹשְׁבִים כָּל מִינֵי מְנוּחָה בַּתְּפִלָּה
And we enumerate all expressions of rest in the prayer
שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
corresponding to our father Jacob, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהוּא זָכָה לְעִיקַּר הַמְּנוּחָה
who merited the fundamental essence of rest,
שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת "וַיִּחַן" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה):
concerning whom Shabbat observance is stated in 'and he encamped' (as written in Bereishit Rabbah): "
מְנוּחַת אַהֲבָה וּנְדָבָה" כָּאָמוּר;
'a rest of love and magnanimity,' as stated; "
מְנוּחַת אֱמֶת וֶאֱמוּנָה"
– 'a rest of truth and faith'—
עַל פִּי מַה שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, רל עַמּוּד א):
based on what is written (Zohar Part III, 230a): "
אִיהוּ אֱמֶת וְאִיהִי אֱמוּנָה",
'He is Truth and she is Faith,'
שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הִכִּיר הַיִּחוּד בְּמִדַּת אֱמֶת
for our father Jacob, peace be upon him, recognized the divine Unity in the attribute of Truth: "
אַתָּה הוּא עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם, אַתָּה הוּא מִשֶּׁנִּבְרָא",
'You are He before the world was created, You are He after the world was created,'
שֶׁהוּא מֶרְכָּבָה לְשֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה שֶׁמּוֹרֶה עַל זֶה: הָיָה, הֹוֶה וְיִהְיֶה.
he being the Chariot to the Tetragrammaton which signifies this: Was, Is, and Will Be.
וּבָנָיו כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה זוֹכִין רַק עַל יְדֵי שֵׁם אֲדֹנָי
And his children, the Congregation of Israel in this world, merit solely through the divine Name Adonai,
וְזָכִין לְהַמְּנוּחָה עַל יְדֵי אֱמוּנָה;
and attain rest through faith; "
מְנוּחָה שְׁלֵמָה שֶׁאַתָּה רוֹצֶה בָּהּ"
– 'a complete rest that You desire'—
שֶׁיְּהֵא הַמְּנוּחָה בִּקְדוּשָׁתוֹ,
that rest be rooted in His holiness,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "יַכִּירוּ בָנֶיךָ וְיֵדְעוּ כִּי מֵאִתְּךָ הִיא מְנוּחָתָם",
as written: 'Your children shall recognize and know that from You is their rest,'
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "הַמַּנְחִיל לְעַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּקְדוּשָׁתוֹ וְגוֹמֵר",
and as written: 'Who bequeaths unto His people Israel in His holiness, etc.,' "
וְעַל מְנוּחָתָם יַקְדִּישׁוּ"
– 'and upon their rest they shall sanctify Your Name'—
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "שֶׁבַח יְקָר וְכוּלֵי" וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ.
as written 'praise, glory, etc.,' and as we have explained.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ מִתְפַּלְּלִין: "וְהַנְחִילֵנוּ ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ וְכוּלֵי וְיָנוּחוּ בָהּ וְכוּלֵי"
And afterwards we pray: 'And bequeath unto us, Hashem our God, etc., and let them rest upon it, etc.'
עַל מַדְרֵגַת הַמְּנוּחָה,
upon the qualitative rung of this rest,
לְהַרְגִּישׁ בְּכָל פַּעַם נִיחָא יוֹתֵר,
to experience in each instance greater tranquility,
שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּזֶה הַרְבֵּה מַדְרֵיגוֹת כָּאָמוּר.
since there are numerous gradations in this, as stated.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Bereshit 78:196-79:206: ‘R. Simeon said further: ‘It is on this account that, as we have learnt, Sabbath is a mirror of the future world. For this same reason, too, the Sabbatical year and the Jubilee mirror one another. This additional soul descends from the mystic force implied in the word zachor (remember) upon the tabernacle of peace, being taken from the future world, and the tabernacle gives it to the holy people, who are gladdened by it and enabled to forget all worldly matters and all their troubles and sorrows, thus realising the words of the prophet, “on the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy trouble, and from the hard service, etc.” (Is. 14, 3).’

paragraphs.text: Temurah 16a:16: “The Gemara interprets this verse. The phrase: “If You will bless me indeed,” means that he prayed for a blessing with regard to Torah. “And enlarge my border,” means that he prayed for a blessing with regard to students. “And that Your hand be with me,” that my studies not be forgotten from my heart. “And that You will work deliverance from evil [mera’ati],” that I will find friends [re’im] like me. “That it may not pain me,” that the evil inclination should not grow stronger and prevent me from studying Torah. Othniel further prayed: If You do so, good; and if not, I will go depressed [linsisi] to my grave and the netherworld. Immediately, God answered him, as the verse states: “And God granted him that which he requested.””

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 5a:2: “Incidental to the verse, “Tremble, and do not sin,” the Gemara mentions that Rabbi Levi bar Ḥama said that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: One should always incite his good inclination against his evil inclination, i.e., that one must constantly struggle so that his evil inclination does not lead him to transgression, as it is stated: "Tremble, and do not sin." If one succeeds and subdues his evil inclination, excellent, but if he does not succeed in subduing it, he should study Torah, as alluded to in the verse: “Say to your heart.” If he subdues his evil inclination, excellent; if not, he should recite Shema, which contains the acceptance of the yoke of God, and the concept of reward and punishment, as it is stated in the verse: “Upon your bed,” which alludes to Shema, where it says: “When you lie down.” If he subdues his evil inclination, excellent; if not, he should remind himself of the day of death, whose silence is alluded to in the continuation of the verse: “And be still, Selah.””

paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 129b:7: “Rav Ashi explains his previous comment: Didn’t Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Avya, send the following ruling in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka? If a person on his deathbed said: My property is given to you, and after you to so-and-so, and the first recipient was fit to inherit from him, the second gets nothing in place of the first, i.e., he does not receive the property after the first one dies, as this formulation employed by the owner was not one of a gift; rather, it was a formulation of inheritance, and inheritance has no end, i.e., it cannot be stopped. Therefore, since the first recipient acquired it as inheritance, his heirs inherit it from him, and it cannot be taken by the second one. Therefore, the baraita is irreconcilable with the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka.”

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 79:6: ““And he encamped [vayiḥan] before the city” – he graced [ḥanan] the leadership of the city, he began sending them gifts. Another matter, “and he encamped [vayiḥan] before the city” – he began establishing markets and selling at low prices. That is what they say, that a person must show gratitude to a place from which he benefits. Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai and Rabbi Elazar his son were hiding in a cave for thirteen years during the days of persecution. They would eat withered carobs until they broke out in sores. After thirteen years, he [Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai] emerged and sat at the cave entrance. He saw a certain hunter standing and hunting birds. When Rabbi Shimon would hear a Divine Voice from Heaven: ‘Freedom, freedom,’ it would escape. But when he would hear a Divine Voice saying: ‘Killing,’ it would be hunted and trapped. He said: ‘Were it not for Heaven, a bird would not be hunted; the soul of a person, all the more so.’ He went out and found that matters were calm, and that the edict had been abrogated. They came and bathed in that heated bathhouse in Tiberias. His son said to him: ‘Tiberias has afforded us so much benefit, and we are not purifying it from the dead?’ He said: ‘We must perform an act of good just as our ancestors would, as they would establish markets and sell at low prices.’ He said: ‘We need to purify Tiberias.’ What did he do? He took a mandrake. He would cut the mandrake, cast the cuttings, and scatter them in the street. Every place where there was a corpse, it would rise, and they would move it and take it out of the city. And every place where there was no impurity, the mandrake would remain, and it would indicate which was a place of purity and which was a place of impurity until the time that they purified it from all the corpses. A certain Samaritan ignoramus saw him and said: ‘Will I not go and mock this Jewish elder?’ Some say it was in the wicker basket market, and some said it was the sack market. He took a corpse and concealed it in one of the streets that had been purified. In the morning, he went and said to them: ‘You said that ben Yoḥai had purified Tiberias. Come and see this corpse.’ [Variant reading: He went to him, he said to him: ‘Did you not purify such and such street?’ He said to him: ‘Yes.’ He said to him: ‘And if I produce corpses after you?’ He said to him: ‘Pull and show it.’] Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai saw through the Divine spirit that he placed it there. He said: ‘I decree that the one who is above shall descend, and the one who is below shall ascend,’ and so it was. He ascended and sat in his house. He passed by the Tower of Colors and heard the voice of Nakai the scribe. He said: ‘Did you not say that bar Yoḥai purified Tiberias? But they say that they found a corpse.’ He said: ‘Let him come to me, if I do not have at my disposal halakhot as numerous as the hair on my head regarding Tiberias, that it is pure, with the exception of this-and-that place. You were not with us in the quorum when it was purified. You breached the fence of the Sages, and in your regard it is written: “One who breaches a fence, a serpent will bite him”’ (Ecclesiastes 10:8). He [Nakai the scribe] immediately became a pile of bones. He [Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai] passed in the Beit Nekofa Valley. He saw a person standing and gathering the sefichin of the Sabbatical year. He said to him: ‘Is this not the sefichin of the Sabbatical year?’ He said to him: ‘But is it not you who permitted it? Did we not learn: Rabbi Shimon says: All the sefichin are permitted except for the sefichin of cabbage, as there is nothing like it in the vegetables of the field.’ He said to him: ‘But do my colleagues not disagree with me? You breached the fence of the Sages, and “one who breaches a fence, a serpent will bite him.”’ And so it was for him. Another matter, “and he encamped before the city” – he entered on Friday near sunset, while it was still day, and established Shabbat boundaries while it was still day. That is to say: Jacob observed Shabbat before it was given.”

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 141:1: “But in truth, the opposite occurs: through this the Holy One, blessed be He, establishes that desire forever. When, amid concealment, he realizes that Hashem’s face is hidden from him and beseeches Hashem to illuminate him, he is already no longer in concealment. Concerning this it is said: The goal of knowledge is that we do not know. This is called humility, and it is the greatest level, as is known. It says, “The humble shall inherit the land”: inheritance has no interruption. Thus concerning Moshe our teacher, who was humbler than every person, it says, “His eye did not grow dim”—his spiritual attainments suffered no interruption.”

paragraphs.text:
Duties of the Heart, Fourth Treatise on Trust 7:15-17: “If his recognition of God grows stronger, he will place his trust in Him amid all the means, difficult and easy alike, and will intend, in occupying himself with them, to serve God and keep His commandments.

When his recognition of the Creator’s compassion toward His creatures grows stronger still, he will willingly accept whatever God decrees for him—in his heart and speech, outwardly and inwardly. He will rejoice in everything God has done for him: death and life, poverty and wealth, health and sickness. He will not yearn for something other than what God has chosen for him, and will desire only what God has desired for him.

He gives himself over to God and casts his soul and body upon His judgment. He will not prefer one condition over another or choose a worldly condition other than the one he is in, as one of those who trust said: “I have never awakened in one condition and desired another.””

וְאִם תֶּחֱזַק הַכָּרָתוֹ בֵּאלֹהִים יוֹתֵר יָשִׁיב בִּטְחוֹנוֹ אֵלָיו בְּכָל הַסִּבּוֹת הַקָּשָׁה מֵהֶן וְהַקַּלָּה וִיכַוֵּן בְּהִתְעַסְּקוֹ בָּהֶן לַעֲבוֹדַת הָאֱלֹהִים וְלִשְׁמֹר מִצְווֹתָיו.

וְכַאֲשֶׁר תֶּחֱזַק הַכָּרָתוֹ יוֹתֵר מִזֶּה בְּחֶמְלַת הַבּוֹרֵא עַל בְּרוּאָיו יִרְצֶה בְּמָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מִגְּזֵרַת הָאֱלֹהִים לוֹ בְּלִבּוֹ וּבִלְשׁוֹנוֹ וּבְנִרְאֵהוּ וּבְנִסְתָּרוֹ וְיִשְׂמַח בְּכָל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה לוֹ הָאֱלֹהִים מִמָּוֶת וְחַיִּים וְרִישׁ וָעֹשֶׁר וּבְרִיאוּת וְחֹלִי לֹא יִכְסֹף לְזוּלַת מָה שֶׁבָּחַר לוֹ הָאֱלֹהִים וְלֹא יִרְצֶה אֶלָּא מָה שֶׁרָצָה לוֹ.

וְנִמְסָר אֶל הָאֱלֹהִים וּמַשְׁלִיךְ נַפְשׁוֹ וְגוּפוֹ אֶל דִּינוֹ. וְלֹא יַגְבִּיר עִנְיָן עַל עִנְיָן וְלֹא יִבְחַר זוּלַת מָה שֶׁהוּא בּוֹ מֵעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָמוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר אֶחָד מִן הַבּוֹטְחִים לֹא הִשְׁכַּמְתִּי מֵעוֹלָם בְּעִנְיָן וְהִתְאַוֵּיתִי לְזוּלָתוֹ.
